anomalies.observed: In the 'Water Height Sensor' block the TF-Luna LiDAR symbol PR1 is drawn with solid wires (and a decoupling cap C1) connecting its VCC/SDA/SCL/GND pins through the 6-pin header H1 directly onto the +5V rail, GND, and the I2C_SDA / I2C_SCL nets. PR1 carries no DNP/no-connect marking, unlike the optional PR5/PR6 sensors which are crossed out.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the LiDAR is intentionally excluded from this build: 'its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net' and 'all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.' The wired water-level interface is the ultrasonic scheme, not a LiDAR on the I2C bus.

evidence.quote: §4.3 ... the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.
§6 Known Limitations ... TF-Luna LiDAR is unwired ... its pins are typed free, it is marked on_board: no, and it has no corresponding firmware code.
Sheet 1, 'Water Height Sensor': PR1 LIDAR pins VCC/SDA/SCL/GND wired to H1, which is connected to +5V, GND, I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL (no no-connect markers, no DNP cross).

anomalies.impact: A 5 V I2C rangefinder that the design deliberately leaves unconnected is now bridged onto the 3.3 V main I2C bus (with 2.2 k pull-ups). This loads/level-conflicts the bus, can introduce an address collision, and changes the water-level sensing path from the intended ultrasonic GPIO scheme to an unexpected LiDAR, so the board behaves differently from the reference design.
